command: llvm-mc -triple=x86_64 -filetype=obj research/evidence/experiments/EXP-0041/P16.asm -o out.o && llvm-objcopy -O binary --only-section=.text out.o out.bin
notes: Sixteen no-displacement SSE memory instructions, eight legacy and eight VEX/EVEX. The legacy half fills all four windows: low/low (`0f 28 11`), high `xmm`/low base (`44 0f 28 09`), low `xmm`/high base (`41 0f 28 11`) and both high (`45 0f 28 11`), each in both directions, with the register and base low bits non-zero (`%xmm2`, `%rcx`, `%xmm9`/`%xmm10`, `%r9`). The VEX half shows the two-byte prefix with `R̄` set (`c5 78 28 02`) and the three-byte prefix with `R̄` and `B̄` both set (`c4 41 78 28 13`). EVEX keeps six bytes and varies `P0`: `f1` low/low, `d1` high base, `71` high register, `51` both. No instruction has a displacement byte, and neither `%rsp`/`%r12` nor `%rbp`/`%r13` appears: those bases are outside the shape. `input_sha256` is P16.asm (386 bytes, the source above); `output_sha256` is the 72-byte .text.
